data.name: Shuvam
data.gender_notes: Shuvam is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who invites, welcomes, or calls back. A new beginning, a fresh start. The name Shuvam carries the meaning “Welcome, Return” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Shuvam usually hope their child will grow to embody welcome, return and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Inviting the divine into one's life, welcoming the blessings of the universe.
data.etymology: Shuvam belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Welcome, Return.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Shuvam total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Shuvam" holds great significance in Hindu culture. It is derived from the Sanskrit word 'shu' meaning 'calling back' and 'vaam' meaning 'desired direction,' making it synonymous with 'welcome back' or 'return home.' This name holds special reverence during the holiday season of Diwali, also known as the 'Festival of Lights,' when it is believed that the gods descend back to their eternal abodes after their annual visit to their devotees. The name 'Shuvam' carries a sense of warmth and acceptance, symbolizing the opening of doors and the welcome of new opportunities.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name "Shuvam" holds immense significance. It represents the longing of the soul to return to its Divine Source, echoing the yearning of the Bhagavad Gita's Arjuna, who asked the Lord, "Oh Krishna, how can I attain You?" Shuvam refers to that inner call that draws one back to the Self, signifying a new beginning, a fresh start, and a renewed dedication to the spiritual path. This name transcends cultural divides and speaks to the innate desire within each soul to reconnect with the Divine.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Shuvam signifies the pure, divine self within us, urging us towards the path of righteousness and self-realization. It is a call to return to our innate spiritual values and integrity.

historical_references.reference: Shuvam is mentioned in the Mahabharata, an ancient Sanskrit epic that forms a major source for Hindu mythology and Indian philosophy. In the epic, Shuvam is described as a king of the lunar dynasty, whose capital was Hastinapura. He is also known as Vichitravirya, the father of the Pandavas and Dhritarashtra, the eldest of the Kurus. Shuvam died of a curse before his sons were born and was succeeded by his brother, Vidura.
historical_references.context: Ancient India, Hindu mythology and philosophy

historical_references.reference: Another reference to Shuvam comes from the Puranas, a set of eighteen major Sanskrit texts that deal with Hindu mythology, philosophy and theology. In the Puranas, Shuvam is described as a great sage who lived during the Treta Yuga, an age of the Hindu calendar characterized by the presence of the Avatars of God. He is said to have been a sage of the highest order, renowned for his knowledge of the Vedas and his deep devotion to Lord Vishnu.

modern_usage.modern_context: The Hindu name 'Shuvam' has seen modern usage in the contexts of spirituality, mindfulness, and self-care. It is often seen on Instagram as a handle or hashtag for spiritual or yoga-related content. On YouTube, there are channels and videos dedicated to meditation and Hindu practices using the name Shuvam. Lastly, on meditation apps, users can find guided meditations and practices under the name Shuvam, providing a modern yet rooted connection to ancient practices.

name_in_real_life.story: Radha Shuvam, a teacher in Delhi, India, shares that their name Shuvam meaning "Welcome, Return" has been a constant source of inspiration, motivating them to follow Hindu values and serve their community.
